title: Focaccia Barese
instructions:
Focaccia Barese

Bari-style focaccia made with durum semolina, potato, cherry tomatoes, green olives, oregano, and extra-virgin olive oil.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

For the dough
4 cups plus 2 tbsp finely milled durum semolina
about 1 cup warm riced boiled potato
1 1/2 cups warm water
about 2 tsp fresh yeast
2 tsp fine salt
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp extra-virgin olive oil

For the topping
2 cups cherry or grape tomatoes
about 2/3 cup green Bari-style olives
2 tsp dried oregano
1 tsp coarse salt
6 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil for the pan and finishing

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast in about 1/3 cup plus 1 tablespoon warm water.

2. Put the semolina and warm potato in a bowl.

3. Add the yeast water.

4. Gradually add the remaining 1 cup plus 1 tablespoon water.

5. Knead for about 10 minutes.

6. Add the salt.

7. Gradually work in the olive oil.

8. Cover.

9. Let rise in a warm place for 2–3 hours, until doubled.

10. Pour about 1/4 cup olive oil into an iron baking pan.

11. Turn the dough into the pan.

12. Gently stretch it with oiled fingertips.

13. Crush the tomatoes directly over the dough, distributing their juice as well.

14. Press the olives into the surface.

15. Sprinkle with oregano and coarse salt.

16. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

17. Cover.

18. Rest for 30–45 minutes.

19. Preheat a conventional oven to 435°F.

20. Bake on a low rack for 20–25 minutes.

21. Move to the center rack for the final 5 minutes.

Service

Rest for 10 minutes and serve warm.

Chef's note

Generous olive oil under the dough helps create the characteristic crisp bottom crust.

title: Bari Sgagliozze
instructions:
Bari Sgagliozze

Fried polenta triangles that are crisp outside and soft inside.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

4 1/4 cups water
1 1/2 cups instant polenta
1 1/3 tsp fine salt, divided
4 1/4 cups peanut oil for frying

Preparation

1. Bring the water to a boil.

2. Add about 3/4 teaspoon salt.

3. Slowly stream in the polenta while stirring continuously.

4. Cook for 3–4 minutes or according to the package directions.

5. Pour the polenta into a rectangular pan.

6. Smooth to about 3/8 inch thick.

7. Cool for 4–5 hours.

8. Unmold the polenta.

9. Cut first into squares and then into triangles.

10. Heat the oil to 355°F.

11. Fry 3–4 triangles at a time.

12. Turn after several minutes.

13. Continue until deeply golden and crisp.

14. Drain on paper towels.

15. Sprinkle with the remaining salt.

Service

Serve immediately.

Chef's note

The polenta must be completely cold and firm before cutting or the triangles can break apart in the oil.

instructions:
Bari Popizze

Very soft Bari-style yeasted dough fritters fried by the spoonful.

Yield: about 30 pieces

2 cups plus 2 tbsp water, room temperature
about 2 tsp fresh yeast

1. Put the flour in a large bowl.

3. Add it to the flour.

4. Gradually add the remaining water.

5. Add the sugar.

6. Add the salt.

8. Continue until fluid, elastic, and uniform.

9. Cover.

Vigorous mixing incorporates air into the dough and contributes to the light interior of the popizze.

title: Salento Pittule
instructions:
Salento Pittule

Soft Salento-style yeasted dough fritters fried until puffed and golden.

Yield: about 50 pieces

Ingredients

4 cups plus 2 tbsp all-purpose flour
2 cups plus 2 tbsp water, room temperature
about 2 tsp fresh yeast
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
4 1/4 cups peanut or high-oleic sunflower oil for frying

Preparation

1. Put the flour in a large bowl.

2. Crumble the yeast into the flour.

3. Add the water gradually.

4. Mix with a sturdy spatula or your hands.

5. Add the salt halfway through mixing.

6. Continue adding the water.

7. Work vigorously for several minutes until the batter is elastic, uniform, soft, and sticky.

8. Cover.

9. Let rise for about 2 hours, until clearly increased in volume.

10. Heat the oil to 340–355°F.

11. Wet or oil two spoons.

12. Scoop small portions of dough.

13. Slide them into the oil.

14. Fry only a few at a time for about 2–3 minutes.

15. Turn during frying.

16. Drain on paper towels.

Serve immediately.

Chef's note

Do not add flour after rising. The dough should remain very soft to produce light, airy pittule.

instructions:
Gratinated Mussels

Puglian mussels gratinated with breadcrumbs, Pecorino, garlic, parsley, and oregano.

Yield: 4 servings

1 tsp dried oregano
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil

Preparation

2. Put them in a saucepan with 1 garlic clove.

3. Cover and cook until they open.

5. Remove the empty half of each shell.

6. Strain the mussel liquid carefully.

instructions:
Polpo alla Pignata

Salento octopus slowly cooked in earthenware with tomatoes, potatoes, onion, garlic, white wine, parsley, and chile.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1 cleaned octopus, about 2 1/4 lb
3 1/3 cups cherry tomatoes
about 3 1/3 cups potato chunks
1 red onion, sliced
1 garlic clove, minced
1 small chile
1/2 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp dry white wine
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
3/4 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Rinse and dry the octopus.

2. Cut the head and tentacles into large pieces.

3. Peel the potatoes.

4. Cut them into even chunks.

5. Halve the cherry tomatoes.

6. Heat the olive oil in an earthenware pot or heavy saucepan.

7. Add the onion, garlic, and chile.

8. Cook for 4–5 minutes.

9. Add the octopus.

10. Sauté for 3–4 minutes.

11. Pour in the wine.

12. Let the alcohol evaporate for 2 minutes.

13. Add the tomatoes and potatoes.

14. Cover.

15. Bring to a gentle boil without adding water.

16. Reduce the heat.

17. Cook for about 1 hour, stirring gently every 15 minutes.

18. Add the salt only near the end.

19. Turn off the heat.

20. Add the parsley.

21. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.

Service

Serve very hot with toasted bread.

Chef's note

The octopus should cook in its own released liquid. Added water dilutes the sauce and is unnecessary if the pot remains covered.

Alici Arraganate

Puglian baked anchovies with stale bread, garlic, parsley, capers, oregano, vinegar, and olive oil.

1/2 cup finely chopped fresh parsley

1 tsp dried oregano, optional
1 tbsp wine vinegar
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Clean the anchovies, removing the heads and innards.

2. Butterfly them and remove the central bones.

3. Rinse briefly.

4. Dry very thoroughly.

5. Lightly grease an earthenware or baking dish with 1 tablespoon olive oil.

6. Arrange the fillets in a radial pattern.

7. Crumble the bread coarsely.

8. Mix it with the garlic, parsley, capers, oregano, and pepper.

9. Scatter the mixture over the anchovies.

10. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

11. Sprinkle with the vinegar.

12. Bake in a preheated 350°F oven for 15 minutes.

Serve hot or cold.

Chef's note

Taste before adding salt; the capers and anchovies can provide enough salinity on their own.

instructions:
Onion Calzone

Bari-style calzone filled with sponsali onions, olives, raisins, anchovies, and cheese.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the dough
3 1/3 cups all-purpose flour
1 cup plus 1 tbsp warm water
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp dry white wine
about 2 1/2 tsp fresh yeast
3 tbsp plus 1 tsp extra-virgin olive oil
1 1/3 tsp fine salt

For the filling
about 6 cups sliced sponsali or mild spring onions
1/3 cup raisins
about 1/3 cup rinsed salt-packed anchovies
1/2 cup finely grated Parmigiano or Pecorino
30 pitted black olives
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1/4 cup water
2/3 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Dissolve the yeast in the warm water.

2. Put the flour in a bowl.

3. Add the yeast water, wine, and olive oil.

4. Knead for about 15 minutes.

5. Add the salt during the final minutes.

6. Form a ball.

7. Cover.

8. Let rise for about 2 hours.

9. Soak the raisins in warm water for 10 minutes.

10. Drain and dry.

11. Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet.

12. Add the sponsali.

13. Add the water.

14. Cook over medium-low heat for about 30 minutes.

15. Add the salt and pepper.

16. Add the cheese, olives, raisins, and anchovies.

17. Continue cooking until the pan is completely dry.

18. Cool completely.

19. Divide the dough into two pieces.

20. Roll into two thin 11-inch disks.

21. Line a pan with the first disk.

22. Add the cooled filling.

23. Cover with the second disk.

24. Seal and fold the edges.

25. Bake in a preheated 445°F oven for at least 30 minutes, until golden.

26. Broil for 1–2 minutes if needed.

Service

Rest for 15 minutes and serve warm.

Chef's note

The filling must be completely dry and cool before it goes into the dough or the bottom crust will stay damp.

instructions:
Scapece Gallipolina

Gallipoli fried small fish layered with stale bread soaked in saffron vinegar.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

1 3/4 lb small frying fish
about 20 cups coarse stale bread crumb
4 1/4 cups white-wine vinegar
3 packets saffron, about 1/2 tsp threads or powder
1 cup durum or all-purpose flour
4 1/4 cups extra-virgin olive oil for frying
1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Dry the small fish thoroughly.

2. Coat lightly in flour.

3. Shake off the excess.

4. Heat the oil to 350°F.

5. Fry the fish in batches until golden.

6. Drain on paper towels.

7. Season with salt.

8. Cool completely.

9. Pour the vinegar into a large bowl.

10. Dissolve the saffron in it.

11. Crumble the stale bread.

12. Moisten it thoroughly with the saffron vinegar until fully saturated.

13. Make one layer of soaked bread in a tall container.

14. Cover with a thin layer of fried fish.

15. Repeat the layers until all ingredients are used.

16. Finish with a bread layer.

17. Cover.

18. Refrigerate for at least 24 hours.

Service

Serve cold or at room temperature.

Chef's note

The 24-hour rest is essential because it allows the saffron vinegar to penetrate both the bread and fish and develop the traditional flavor.

title: Palermo Arancine
instructions:
Palermo Arancine

Round Palermo rice balls with saffron rice, meat-and-pea ragù, batter, and breadcrumbs.

Yield: about 20 arancine

Ingredients

For the rice
5 cups Originario or short-grain rice
8 1/2 cups water
about 1 1/2 tbsp vegetable bouillon concentrate
2 saffron packets, about 1/8 tsp
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

For the ragù
1 1/8 lb ground beef
1 onion, finely chopped
4 1/4 cups tomato sauce
1 1/3 cups peas
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp dry white wine
1 bay leaf
3/4 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

For the optional center
about 1 1/4 cups diced well-drained primosale or mozzarella

For the batter and coating
1 2/3 cups all-purpose flour
1 1/4 cups cold water
1 large egg
1/2 tsp fine salt
2 1/2 cups breadcrumbs

For frying
4 1/4 cups peanut oil

Preparation

1. Put the rice, water, vegetable bouillon, and saffron in a large saucepan.

2. Add the salt and pepper.

3. Bring to a boil.

4. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring frequently, until the rice absorbs all of the water.

5. Spread the rice in a thin layer on a baking sheet.

6. Cool completely.

7. For the ragù, heat the olive oil in a saucepan.

8. Add the onion.

9. Cook for 5 minutes.

10. Add the ground beef.

11. Brown for 7–8 minutes.

12. Pour in the wine.

13. Let the alcohol evaporate.

14. Add the tomato sauce, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.

15. Cook over low heat for 30 minutes.

16. Add the peas.

17. Continue for another 15 minutes, until the ragù is very thick.

18. Remove the bay leaf.

19. Cool completely.

20. Make the batter by whisking the flour, water, egg, and salt until smooth and fluid.

21. Lightly wet your hands.

22. Take one portion of rice and make a hollow in your palm.

23. Put about 1 heaping tablespoon ragù in the center and, if using, one cube of primosale or mozzarella.

24. Cover with more rice.

25. Compact into a ball.

26. Dip each arancina in the batter.

27. Let excess batter drip away.

28. Coat in breadcrumbs.

29. Heat the oil to 350°F.

30. Fry only a few at a time for 5–7 minutes, turning until evenly golden.

31. Drain on paper towels.

Service

Rest for 3–5 minutes and serve hot.

Chef's note

The rice and ragù must be completely cold before shaping; warm components make the arancine difficult to compact.

Catania Arancini

title: Panelle
instructions:
Panelle

Palermo chickpea fritters flavored with parsley and black pepper.

Yield: about 10 panelle

1 cup chickpea flour

3/4 tsp fine salt
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
4 1/4 cups peanut oil for frying
1 lemon, optional for serving

Preparation

1. Put the chickpea flour, water, salt, pepper, and parsley in a saucepan.

2. Whisk thoroughly while still cold.

3. Set the pan over low heat.

4. Cook, stirring continuously, for 15–20 minutes.

5. Continue until the mixture is very thick, smooth, and pulls away from the sides.

6. Immediately spread the hot mixture over flat plates or a smooth surface in a thin layer.

7. Cool for about 15 minutes.

8. Carefully lift off the panelle.

9. Cut into the desired shape.

instructions:
Palermo Potato Croquettes

Palermo potato croquettes made only with potatoes, parsley, and mint, fried without breading.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

about 1 lb floury mature potatoes
1/3 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
3 tbsp finely chopped fresh mint
3/4 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper
4 1/4 cups peanut oil for frying

Preparation

1. Wash the potatoes.

2. Put them whole and unpeeled in a pot of cold salted water.

3. Bring to a boil.

4. Cook until tender.

5. Drain.

6. Cool completely in a colander, preferably overnight.

7. Peel the cold potatoes.

8. Pass them through a potato ricer.

9. Add the parsley, mint, salt, and pepper.

10. Mix quickly without overworking the potatoes.

11. Lightly oil your hands.

12. Shape into elongated croquettes.

13. Arrange on a tray lined with a clean kitchen towel.

14. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

15. Heat the oil to 375°F.

16. Fry only a few croquettes at a time for about 2 minutes, until deeply golden.

17. Drain with a slotted spoon.

Service

Serve immediately.

Chef's note

Cooling the potatoes for many hours dries them and concentrates the starch, allowing the croquettes to hold together without eggs or breading.

Sfincione Palermitano

Palermo sfincione topped with stewed onion, tomato, salted sardines, caciocavallo, breadcrumbs, and oregano.

2 cups plus 2 tbsp tomato sauce

2. Add the onion.

3. Add the water.

4. Stew for about 10 minutes, until soft.

5. Add the sardines.

6. Stir until they dissolve.

7. Add the tomato sauce.

8. Season with salt and pepper.

9. Cook for about 30 minutes, until thick.

10. Turn off the heat.

11. Stir in the breadcrumbs and oregano.

12. Cool completely.

13. Grease a baking pan with about 1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon olive oil.

14. Stretch the dough with your fingers.

15. Press the caciocavallo lightly into the dough.

16. Cover with the cooled sauce.

17. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

18. Let rise for about 20 minutes.

title: Sarde a Beccafico
instructions:
Sarde a Beccafico

Sicilian sardines rolled with breadcrumbs, raisins, pine nuts, anchovies, parsley, and bay leaves.

Yield: 4 servings

1 2/3 lb fresh sardines
about 3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp breadcrumbs

1/3 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
8 bay leaves
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, divided
2 tbsp lemon juice
2/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Soak the raisins in warm water for 15 minutes.

2. Drain and dry.

3. Clean the sardines, removing the heads, innards, and bones.

4. Butterfly them.

5. Rinse briefly.

6. Dry thoroughly.

7. Reserve 1 tablespoon breadcrumbs.

8. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a skillet.

9. Add the remaining breadcrumbs.

10. Toast until lightly golden.

11. Remove from the heat.

12. Add the raisins, pine nuts, parsley, anchovies, salt, and pepper.

13. Mix well.

14. Put a small amount of filling on each sardine.

15. Roll from the widest end toward the tail.

16. Arrange the rolls in a baking dish, alternating them with bay leaves.

17. Sprinkle with the reserved breadcrumbs.

18. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

19. Bake in a preheated 425°F oven for 15–20 minutes.

20. Drizzle with lemon juice immediately after baking.

Service

Serve hot or warm.

Chef's note

Do not overfill the sardines; a compact roll holds its shape better during baking.

Eggplant Caponata

Sicilian sweet-and-sour eggplant caponata with celery, tomato, olives, capers, raisins, and pine nuts.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1 round purple eggplant, about 1 1/2 lb
1 celery stalk
2/3 cup peeled tomatoes

1 tbsp sugar

2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil

Preparation

1. Cut the eggplant into even cubes.

2. Put it in a colander.

3. Sprinkle with the coarse salt.

4. Place a weight on top.

5. Let drain for about 2 hours.

6. Rinse briefly.

7. Dry very thoroughly.

8. Heat the peanut oil to 350°F.

9. Fry the eggplant in small batches until golden.

10. Drain on paper towels.

11. Soak the raisins in cold water for 10 minutes.

12. Drain.

13. Blanch the celery for 3 minutes.

14. Drain and cut into pieces.

15. Chop the tomatoes and halve the olives.

16. Heat the extra-virgin olive oil in a wide skillet.

17. Add the celery.

18. Sauté for 2–3 minutes.

19. Add the capers, raisins, olives, pine nuts, tomatoes, and basil.

20. Cook for 5 minutes.

21. Add the fried eggplant.

22. Season with fine salt and pepper.

23. Cook for another 3 minutes.

24. Dissolve the sugar in the vinegar.

25. Pour it into the skillet.

26. Increase the heat slightly.

27. Cook for another 10 minutes, until the sharp vinegar aroma softens.

Service

Rest for at least 2 hours and serve at room temperature.

Chef's note

Caponata improves after resting because the sweet-and-sour dressing penetrates the vegetables and the flavors balance.

title: Stigghiola

Stigghiola

Palermo-style lamb intestines wrapped around scallions and parsley stems and grilled over coals.

Ingredients

1 unwaxed lemon
1/2 cup fresh parsley with intact stems
4 small scallions
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Rinse the intestines under cold running water.

2. Fill a bowl with cold water.

3. Add half of the salt and the juice of half the lemon.

4. Soak the intestines for 15 minutes.

5. Rinse very thoroughly again.

6. Dry.

7. Clean the scallions and keep them whole.

8. Divide the parsley stems into four small bundles.

9. Pair one scallion with one parsley bundle.

10. Wrap one portion of intestine tightly around the aromatics from end to end.

11. Repeat to make 4 stigghiola.

12. Prepare medium-hot coals with no direct flame.

13. Put the stigghiola on the grill.

14. Cook for 15–20 minutes.

15. Turn frequently for even browning.

16. Season gradually with the remaining salt and pepper.

17. Continue until the exterior is deeply browned and crisp and no soft or wet sections remain.

Service

Serve immediately with wedges from the remaining lemon.

Chef's note

Use steady medium heat without flames. Dripping fat can cause flare-ups that burn the outside before the interior cooks completely.

title: Ribollita
instructions:
Ribollita

Tuscan bean-and-vegetable soup with cannellini beans, Tuscan kale, Savoy cabbage, and stale bread.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

4 cups cooked cannellini beans
7 cups bean cooking liquid or water

1 potato, diced
about 3 cups sliced Tuscan kale
about 4 cups sliced Savoy cabbage

about 4 cups thinly sliced stale Tuscan-style bread

1 1/4 tsp fine salt, divided
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Blend half of the beans with 1 cup of the measured cooking liquid.

2. Reserve the purée and the remaining whole beans separately.

3. Heat 3 tablespoons olive oil in a large pot.

4. Add the onion and garlic with about 1/3 teaspoon salt.

5. Cook over low heat for 5 minutes.

6. Add the carrots, celery, and potato.

7. Stir for 3 minutes.

8. Add the Tuscan kale and Savoy cabbage.

9. Pour in the remaining cooking liquid.

10. Add the tomato paste, remaining salt, and pepper.

11. Bring to a gentle simmer.

12. Cook for about 40 minutes, stirring occasionally.

13. Add the bean purée.

14. Cook for another 20 minutes, stirring frequently.

15. Add the whole beans.

16. Cook for another 10 minutes.

17. Add the sliced bread.

18. Stir and cook for another 10 minutes.

19. Turn off the heat.

20. Rest for at least 30 minutes.

Service

Finish with the remaining olive oil. For traditional ribollita, cool completely, refrigerate, and reheat the next day until the soup returns to a simmer.

Chef's note

The cannellini purée thickens the soup naturally; stir frequently after adding it so the bottom does not catch.

Maremma Acquacotta

4 medium white or yellow onions, thinly sliced
1 whole leafy celery bunch, about 4 cups sliced
4 1/4 cups peeled tomatoes
4 basil leaves
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil

4 large eggs
2/3 cup finely grated Parmigiano

1 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp dried chile

Preparation

1. Put the onions and celery in a large pot.

2. Add the water, olive oil, salt, chile, and basil.

3. Bring to a gentle simmer.

4. Cook uncovered over medium-low heat until nearly all of the water has evaporated and the vegetables are very soft, about 35–45 minutes.

5. Add the peeled tomatoes, crushing them with a spoon.

6. Add 2 cups plus 2 tablespoons hot water.

7. Cook for another 20 minutes.

8. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

9. Make four small spaces in the soup.

10. Crack one egg into each.

11. Cover.

12. Cook for 3–5 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks remain soft.

13. Put one slice of stale bread in each bowl.

14. Sprinkle the bread with Parmigiano.

Service

Ladle the soup over the bread and place one poached egg in each serving.

Chef's note

The long first cooking concentrates the sweetness of the onions and celery; do not add the tomatoes until the initial water has nearly evaporated.

Casentino Acquacotta

Pappa al Pomodoro

Tuscan tomato-and-bread soup with stale bread, peeled tomatoes, garlic, basil, and extra-virgin olive oil.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

3 1/3 cups crushed canned peeled tomatoes
2 garlic cloves
1 small dried chile, crumbled
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, divided
4 thick slices stale Tuscan-style bread
1 cup hot water
20 basil leaves
1 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Put the bread in cold water.

2. Soak for about 10 minutes.

3. Heat 3 tablespoons olive oil in a pot.

4. Add the garlic and chile.

5. Cook over low heat for 1 minute.

6. Add the crushed tomatoes.

7. Cook over low heat for 10–15 minutes, until they begin breaking down.

8. Squeeze the bread thoroughly.

9. Crumble it into the tomato sauce.

10. Add the hot water.

11. Add the salt.

12. Cook over low heat for about 10 minutes, stirring vigorously every 2–3 minutes.

13. Turn off the heat.

14. Add the basil.

15. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

16. Rest for at least 1 hour.

Service

Serve warm or at room temperature.

Chef's note

Vigorous stirring during cooking breaks down the bread and creates the thick creamy texture characteristic of pappa al pomodoro.

title: Tuscan Bread Soup
instructions:
Tuscan Bread Soup

Prato-style bread soup with Tuscan kale, Savoy cabbage, chard, cannellini beans, potatoes, and stale bread.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

1 onion, finely chopped
1 garlic clove, minced
2 carrots, diced
2 celery stalks, diced
about 2 cups potato chunks
about 8 cups chopped Savoy cabbage
about 10 cups chopped Tuscan kale
about 6 cups chopped chard
about 2 1/2 cups cooked cannellini beans
1 tbsp tomato paste
1 stale rustic loaf, about 10 cups thinly sliced
5 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
1 cup hot water for the tomato paste
4 1/4 cups water, plus 3 cups plus 3 tbsp bean cooking liquid
1 1/3 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Heat 4 tablespoons olive oil in a large pot.

2. Add the onion and garlic.

3. Cook for 5 minutes.

4. Dilute the tomato paste in the hot water.

5. Pour it into the pot.

6. Add the carrots and celery.

7. Cook for 3 minutes.

8. Add the Tuscan kale and Savoy cabbage.

9. Stir until they begin to wilt.

10. Add the chard and potatoes.

11. Blend three-quarters of the cannellini beans with the bean cooking liquid.

12. Pour the purée into the pot.

13. Add the measured water.

14. Add the salt.

15. Cover.

16. Cook over low heat for about 1 hour.

17. Cut the bread into thin slices.

18. Build 3–4 layers in a serving bowl, alternating bread and hot soup.

19. Finish with the whole cannellini beans.

20. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil.

21. Rest for at least 30 minutes.

Service

Serve warm, or reheat the next day to turn it into ribollita.

Chef's note

Layering the boiling soup over the bread lets it absorb evenly without immediately becoming an indistinct mash.

title: Garfagnana Farro Soup
instructions:
Garfagnana Farro Soup

Tuscan Garfagnana farro soup with beans, potato, cabbage, and aromatic vegetables.

Yield: 4 servings

1 cup dried soaked cannellini or borlotti beans, or about 2 1/2 cups cooked beans

1 carrot, finely chopped

2. Drain and boil in fresh water until tender.

3. Reserve 6 1/3 cups of their cooking liquid.

13. Add the salt.

14. Bring to a gentle simmer.

15. Cook over low heat for 40–50 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes.

17. Rest for 5 minutes.

Service

Chef's note

Farro continues absorbing liquid while the soup rests, so keep the soup slightly looser at the end of cooking.

title: Frantoio-style Soup
instructions:
Frantoio-style Soup

Lucca-hills bean soup with pancetta, seasonal vegetables, wild greens, Tuscan kale, herbs, and stale bread.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

about 5 cups dried beans, soaked for 12 hours and boiled
about 1/2 cup sliced pancetta
about 3 cups mixed wild greens such as sow thistle, borage, and chives
about 2 cups parsley leaves
2 medium leeks
about 1 1/3 cups squash chunks
3 potatoes, cut into chunks
2 small white cabbages, coarsely chopped
3 bunches Tuscan kale, cleaned and chopped
3 small bunches fresh thyme
3 carrots, cut into pieces
5 celery stalks, cut into pieces
1 red onion, coarsely chopped
3 garlic cloves
2 chiles
2 1/2 cups extra-virgin olive oil, divided
1 tsp fennel seeds
3 1/4 qt hot water
36 large cubes stale bread
2 1/2 tsp fine salt
1 1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Coarsely cut all of the vegetables and herbs.

2. Heat about 2 cups plus 2 tablespoons olive oil in a very large pot.

3. Add the pancetta, onion, garlic, leeks, celery, and carrots.

4. Cook for 10 minutes over medium-low heat.

5. Add the squash, potatoes, cabbages, Tuscan kale, wild greens, parsley, thyme, chiles, and fennel seeds.

6. Stir and cook for another 10 minutes, until the vegetables begin to wilt.

7. Add the cooked beans.

8. Pour in 3 1/4 qt hot water.

9. Add the salt.

10. Bring to a gentle simmer.

11. Cook over low heat for about 2 hours, stirring every 15–20 minutes.

12. During the final 30 minutes, uncover if the soup remains too loose.

13. Add the pepper.

14. Put 5–6 large stale-bread cubes in each bowl.

15. Ladle the boiling soup over the bread.

16. Rest for 5 minutes, until the bread softens.

Service

Finish with the remaining olive oil and serve very hot.

Chef's note

The large volume of vegetables requires a very roomy pot; a gentle simmer lets the different vegetables meld without completely breaking down.

title: Carabaccia
instructions:
Carabaccia

Florentine onion soup with carrots, celery, and peas, served over toast with a poached egg.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

3 red onions, diced
3 medium carrots, diced
5 celery stalks, diced
2 cups peas
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp olive oil
4 large eggs
8 slices Tuscan-style bread
1 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Put the onions, carrots, and celery in an earthenware or heavy-bottomed saucepan.

2. Add the olive oil.

3. Add half of the salt.

4. Cover.

5. Cook over medium-low heat for about 1 hour, stirring every 10 minutes.

6. Do not add water; the vegetables should slowly stew in their own juices.

7. Divide the peas into two portions.

8. Boil 1 cup peas for 5 minutes.

9. Drain and reserve.

10. Boil the remaining 1 cup peas for 8 minutes.

11. Blend until smooth.

12. During the final 10 minutes of vegetable cooking, add both the whole peas and pea purée.

13. Add the remaining salt and pepper.

14. Toast the bread.

15. Poach the 4 eggs in barely simmering water for 3–4 minutes.

16. Put 2 toast slices in each bowl.

17. Ladle the soup over the bread.

18. Top each serving with one poached egg.

Service

Serve immediately.

Chef's note

Carabaccia cooks without added water during the first stage; the covered pot traps steam and lets the onions become sweet without scorching.

Garmugia Lucchese

Lucca spring soup with fava beans, peas, ground beef, pancetta, asparagus, and artichokes.

3. Cook for 3–4 minutes.

4. Add the pancetta and ground beef.

5. Brown over high heat for 5–6 minutes.

6. Add the artichokes and chopped asparagus stems.

7. Cook for 3 minutes.

8. Add the fava beans and peas.

9. Pour in the hot broth.

10. Add the salt.

11. Bring to a gentle simmer.

12. Cook for 30–40 minutes.

13. Add the asparagus tips.

15. Add the pepper.

Chef's note

Add the asparagus tips only near the end because they are much more tender than the stems and need far less cooking.

instructions:
Tuscan Kale Soup

Tuscan soup with black kale, cannellini beans, potatoes, aromatic vegetables, and toasted bread.

6. Cook for 7–8 minutes.

7. Add the potatoes.

12. Add the salt.

13. Cover.

14. Cook for 5 minutes.

16. Pour in the remaining broth.

17. Bring to a boil.

18. Reduce the heat.

19. Cover and cook for about 40 minutes.

Castelluccio Lentil Soup

Umbrian Castelluccio lentil soup with aromatic vegetables, optional tomato, and toasted rustic bread.

Preparation

1. Rinse the lentils thoroughly under cold running water.

2. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a pot.

3. Add the carrot, celery, and onion.

4. Cook gently for 7–8 minutes without browning.

5. Add the lentils.

6. Stir for 2 minutes.

7. Add the tomatoes if using.

8. Pour in the water or broth.

9. Bring to a boil.

10. Reduce the heat.

11. Cover with a small vent.

12. Simmer for 40–45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender.

13. Add the salt and pepper during the final 10 minutes.

14. Toast the bread.

15. Rub it with the garlic.

Service

Put one bread slice in each bowl, ladle the hot soup over it, and finish with the remaining olive oil.

Chef's note

Castelluccio lentils have thin skins and do not require soaking; rinse them thoroughly before cooking.

title: Umbrian Farro Soup
instructions:
Umbrian Farro Soup

Umbrian farro-and-bean soup with aromatic vegetables, herbs, tomato paste, and broth.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1 1/2 cups pearled or hulled farro
1 cup dried borlotti or cannellini beans
1 medium yellow onion, finely chopped
1 medium carrot, finely chopped
1 celery stalk, finely chopped
2 garlic cloves
2 tbsp tomato paste
1 rosemary sprig
2 sage leaves
1 bay leaf
6 1/3 cups light vegetable or meat broth
5 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
1 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1 pinch dried chile, optional

Preparation

1. Soak the farro and beans separately in cold water for at least 8 hours.

2. Drain and rinse.

3. Boil the beans in unsalted water for 40–50 minutes, until almost tender.

4. Drain, reserving 2 cups cooking liquid.

5. Heat 3 tablespoons olive oil in a large saucepan.

6. Add the onion, carrot, and celery.

7. Cook for 8–10 minutes.

8. Add the garlic, rosemary, sage, and bay leaf.

9. Cook for 2 minutes.

10. Add the tomato paste.

11. Cook for 1–2 minutes.

12. Add the drained farro.

13. Stir for 2 minutes.

14. Pour in the hot broth and 1 cup bean cooking liquid.

15. Bring to a boil.

16. Cover with a small vent.

17. Cook for 30–35 minutes.

18. Add the beans.

19. Add the salt, pepper, and optional chile.

20. Cook for another 5–10 minutes.

21. Add more bean cooking liquid if needed to adjust the consistency.

22. Remove the herbs.

23. Turn off the heat.

24. Rest for 5 minutes.

Service

Finish with the remaining olive oil and black pepper.

Chef's note

Adding the beans near the end prevents them from breaking apart while the farro finishes cooking.

title: Chickpea and Chestnut Soup
instructions:
Chickpea and Chestnut Soup

Umbrian chickpea and roasted-chestnut soup with tomato, garlic, parsley, and toasted bread.

Yield: 2 servings

Ingredients

1 1/2 cups cooked chickpeas
about 1 1/2 cups cooked peeled chestnuts
1/4 cup plus 1 tbsp tomato passata
2 cups plus 2 tbsp water
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, plus 1 tbsp for serving
1/2 garlic clove, minced
1/4 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
4 slices stale bread
2/3 tsp fine salt
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Cut a slit through the shell of each chestnut.

2. Roast in a 400°F oven for about 20 minutes.

3. Wrap in a kitchen towel for 5 minutes.

4. Peel away both the shell and inner skin.

5. Coarsely chop half of the chestnuts.

6. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a pot.

7. Add the chestnuts, garlic, and parsley.

8. Cook gently for 3–4 minutes.

9. Add the tomato passata.

10. Cook for 3 minutes.

11. Add the chickpeas.

12. Pour in the water.

13. Season with salt and pepper.

14. Bring to a gentle boil.

15. Simmer over low heat for about 1 hour, stirring occasionally.

16. Toast the bread.

Service

Ladle the soup into bowls, add the toast, and finish with the remaining olive oil.

Chef's note

Chopping only part of the chestnuts thickens the soup while leaving some whole pieces for texture.

Cicerchia Soup

14. Add the cicerchie with some of their cooking liquid to the tomato sauce.

15. Continue simmering for 15–20 minutes, until very tender and creamy.

Trasimeno Bean Soup

Preparation

3. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large pot.

4. Add the pancetta and vegetables.

5. Cook over low heat for 6–7 minutes.

7. Cook for 2–3 minutes.

8. Add the beans.

9. Pour in 1 cup water.

10. Bring to a boil.

11. Add the bay leaf.

12. Cook over low heat for about 20 minutes.

13. Add the salt.

14. Continue for another 10 minutes, adding water gradually if needed.

15. Meanwhile, boil the farro in lightly salted water until tender.

16. Drain.

17. Add the farro to the beans.

18. Cook together for 3–4 minutes.

Service

Fava Bean Soup

Dried-fava soup with cavatelli and artichokes flavored with rosemary and marjoram.

2. Drain and rinse.

3. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a saucepan.

5. Cook for 6–7 minutes.

6. Add the fava beans.

7. Stir for 2 minutes.

8. Add the broth.

9. Bring to a boil.

13. Trim the artichokes down to the hearts.

15. Heat the remaining olive oil in a saucepan.

17. Add the artichokes.

18. Sauté for 6–8 minutes, until tender.

19. Cook the cavatelli in salted water until 3 minutes short of al dente.

20. Drain.

21. Add the fava purée and cavatelli to the artichokes.

22. Cook together for about 3 minutes.

23. Adjust the salt and pepper.

Puréeing the fava beans once completely tender creates a creamy base that coats the cavatelli without cream.

Marche Tacconi Soup-style Pasta

Marche pasta made with fava-bean and wheat flours, served with a simple onion-and-fresh-tomato sauce.

Preparation

1. Combine the two flours.

2. Make a well on the work surface.

3. Crack the eggs into the center.

4. Add the salt.

5. Knead for 8–10 minutes, until smooth and elastic.

6. Wrap the dough.

7. Rest for 30 minutes.

8. Roll to about 1/16–1/8 inch thick.

9. Let dry for 10 minutes.

10. Roll the sheet loosely.

11. Cut into strips about 1/4–3/8 inch wide.

12. Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet.

13. Add the onion.

14. Cook for 6–7 minutes.

16. Season with salt and pepper.

17. Cover.

18. Cook for 8–10 minutes.

19. Add the basil.

20. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

21. Cook the tacconi for about 4 minutes, until they float and are tender.

22. Drain.

23. Transfer to the skillet with the sauce.

24. Toss for 1 minute.

Service

Finish with Parmigiano if desired.

Chef's note

Fava-bean flour makes the pasta more fragile than wheat flour alone; resting the dough makes rolling easier.

Abruzzo Chickpea and Chestnut Soup

Teramo May Day soup with dried and fresh legumes, spring vegetables, herbs, pork, mixed pasta, and Pecorino.

2 cups plus 2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
1 1/2 cups tomato passata or crushed fresh tomato

3 1/4 qt hot broth, available for adjusting consistency

Preparation

1. The night before, soak the beans, chickpeas, dried fava beans, and cicerchie separately for 12 hours.

2. Drain and rinse all legumes.

3. Cook each dried-legume variety separately in plenty of water until tender but still intact.

4. Drain, reserving about 2 qt total cooking liquid.

5. Season the cooked legumes with about 1 teaspoon salt, half of the marjoram, half of the mint, and half of the dill.

6. Blanch the pork rind, tail, feet, and ear for 5 minutes.

7. Drain and replace the water.

8. Simmer the pork parts with the prosciutto and mixed soup meat until tender, about 90 minutes.

9. Remove the bones from the feet and tail.

10. Cut all of the meat and rind into small pieces.

11. Reserve 4 1/4 cups meat broth.

12. Separately blanch the turnips, endive, spinach, chicory, chard, and cauliflower only until half cooked.

13. Drain and reserve.

14. Cut the zucchini, potatoes, carrots, artichokes, fennel, leek, celery, and green beans into even pieces.

15. Heat about 1 1/2 cups olive oil in a very large pot.

16. Add the onions and garlic.

17. Cook for 5 minutes.

18. Add the zucchini, potatoes, carrots, artichokes, fennel, leek, celery, and green beans.

19. Add the basil, parsley, marjoram, sage, mint, oregano, dill, bay leaves, thyme, pepper, and cloves.

20. Add the tomato.

21. Cook slowly for 20 minutes.

22. If the pan becomes dry, add 2 cups plus 2 tablespoons reserved broth.

23. Add the cooked legumes, peas, fresh fava beans, and meats.

24. Add the remaining meat broth and 4 1/4 cups legume cooking liquid.

25. Cook for 20 minutes.

26. Add the half-cooked leafy vegetables.

27. Cook for another 15 minutes.

28. Add the remaining salt.

29. Cook the different pastas separately in salted water and drain while very al dente.

30. Add all of the pasta to the Virtù.

31. Boil together for 3–5 minutes.

32. If needed, gradually add the remaining hot broth until thick but still spoonable.

Service

Rest for 10 minutes. Serve with Pecorino and the remaining olive oil.

Chef's note

Virtù depends on cooking each ingredient according to its own timing before the final combination; cooking everything together from the beginning would flatten both texture and flavor.

3. Bring slowly to a boil.

title: Minestra Maritata
instructions:
Minestra Maritata

Campanian wedding soup with pork ribs, sausage, Savoy cabbage, escarole, greens, and Parmigiano rinds.

1 garlic clove

Preparation

1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot.

2. Add the celery, carrot, onion, and garlic.

3. Cook for 7–8 minutes.

4. Remove the garlic.

5. Add the cold water.

6. Cover.

7. Bring to a boil.

8. Reduce the heat and cook for 10–15 minutes.

9. Scrape the Parmigiano rinds thoroughly.

10. Add them to the broth.

11. Add about 3/4 teaspoon salt.

12. Add the ribs and sausages.

13. Return to a boil.

14. Reduce the heat.

15. Cook for 3 hours, skimming foam and fat periodically.

16. Wash the cabbage, escarole, and greens.

17. Chop coarsely.

18. Remove the meats from the broth.

19. Remove the rib bones.

20. Cut the ribs and sausages into pieces.

21. Bring the broth back to a boil.

22. Add all of the greens.

23. Cook for 5–7 minutes.

24. Add the remaining salt only if needed.

25. Return the meats to the pot.

26. Heat for 2 minutes.

Service

Serve very hot with a balanced portion of meat, greens, and broth.

Chef's note

Skimming fat throughout the long cooking keeps the soup rich without making it heavy.

title: Neapolitan Soffritto Soup
instructions:
Neapolitan Soffritto Soup

Neapolitan spicy pork-offal soup with lard, red wine, concentrated tomato, bay, rosemary, and chile.

Yield: 8 servings

Ingredients

4 lb mixed pork offal such as lung, trachea, heart, and spleen
1 tbsp olive oil
7 tbsp lard
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp dry red wine
3 tbsp tomato paste concentrate
1/4 cup water for diluting the concentrate
about 3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp double-concentrated tomato paste
1 bay leaf
1 small chile
1 rosemary sprig
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
2 cups plus 2 tbsp hot water, plus another 2 cups plus 2 tbsp available if needed

Preparation

1. Cut the offal into pieces about 3/4 inch wide.

2. Soak in plenty of fresh water for 2 hours.

3. Change the water at least twice.

4. Drain.

5. Dry very thoroughly.

6. Heat the olive oil and lard in a heavy saucepan.

7. Add the offal.

8. Brown over high heat for 10–15 minutes, stirring often, until deeply colored.

9. Pour in the red wine.

10. Let the alcohol evaporate.

11. Dilute the first tomato concentrate in the measured water.

12. Add it with the remaining concentrated tomato.

13. Add the bay leaf, chile, rosemary, and salt.

14. Cook for 5 minutes.

15. Add the hot water.

16. Bring to a gentle simmer.

17. Reduce the heat.

18. Cover partially.

19. Cook for about 2 hours.

20. Stir every 15 minutes.

21. If the sauce becomes too thick before the offal is tender, add the remaining hot water in 1/2-cup portions.

22. Remove the bay leaf and rosemary.

Service

Serve very hot with rustic bread.

Chef's note

Browning the offal thoroughly before adding tomato and water develops the deep flavor characteristic of soffritto.

title: Neapolitan Mussel Soup
instructions:
Neapolitan Mussel Soup

Neapolitan Holy Thursday seafood soup with octopus, mussels, clams, shrimp, sea snails, friselle, and spicy red “’o russ” oil.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

For the soup
3 1/4 lb octopus
2 1/4 lb very fresh mussels
7/8 lb purged clams
8 whole shrimp or scampi
about 1/2 lb small sea snails
8–12 olive-oil friselle
4 garlic cloves
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil for the separate seafood cooking

For the spicy “’o russ” oil
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
2 dried red chiles, crumbled
2 tbsp tomato paste
1/4 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Prepare the spicy oil first.

2. Put the olive oil, chile, tomato paste, and salt in a heavy small saucepan.

3. Heat over the lowest setting for 15 minutes without letting the tomato paste fry.

4. Stir regularly.

5. Turn off the heat and cool.

6. Bring a large pot of unsalted water to a boil.

7. Dip the octopus tentacles into the boiling water three times to curl them.

8. Lower the entire octopus into the water.

9. Reduce the heat.

10. Cook for 40–45 minutes.

11. Turn off the heat.

12. Rest the octopus in its broth for 10 minutes.

13. Remove and cut into pieces.

14. Reserve the broth.

15. Clean the mussels thoroughly.

16. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil with 1 garlic clove in a skillet.

17. Add the mussels.

18. Cover and cook until they open.

19. Discard any that remain closed.

20. Strain their liquid and add it to the octopus broth.

21. Repeat with the clams using another 1 tablespoon olive oil and 1 garlic clove.

22. Sauté the shrimp or scampi with 1 tablespoon olive oil and 1 garlic clove for 2–3 minutes.

23. Sauté the sea snails with the final 1 tablespoon olive oil and garlic clove for 3–4 minutes.

24. Reheat the octopus broth enriched with the strained shellfish liquids.

25. Dip each frisella in the hot broth for only a few seconds.

26. Arrange 2–3 friselle in each bowl.

27. Add the octopus, mussels, clams, shrimp, and sea snails.

28. Drizzle each serving with 1–2 tablespoons spicy red oil.

Service

Serve immediately while very hot.

Chef's note

The friselle should soften only on the outside while remaining somewhat firm in the center; dip them in the broth for only a few seconds.

Campanian Cicerchia Soup

Campi Flegrei grass-pea soup with guanciale, aromatic vegetables, white wine, cherry tomatoes, and chile.

Ingredients

2 cups dried cicerchie or grass peas

Preparation

1. Check the cicerchie and remove any small stones.

2. Soak in plenty of warm water for 24–48 hours.

3. Change the soaking water at least twice.

4. Drain and rinse thoroughly.

5. Put the cicerchie in a pot with the cold unsalted water.

6. Bring to a boil.

7. Cook over moderate heat for about 2 hours, until tender but not falling apart.

8. Drain only immediately before the final preparation, reserving the measured cooking liquid.

9. Heat the olive oil in a saucepan.

10. Add the guanciale, celery, carrots, onion, and garlic.

11. Brown for 8–10 minutes.

12. Pour in the white wine.

13. Let the alcohol evaporate.

14. Add the cicerchie.

15. Pour in the reserved cooking liquid.

16. Bring to a gentle simmer.

17. Cook over low heat for about 50 minutes.

18. Add the tomatoes, chile, and salt.

19. Continue for another 10 minutes.

Service

Rest for 5 minutes and serve very hot.

Chef's note

Add the salt only near the end so it does not slow the softening of the cicerchie during their long cooking.

Cabbage and Rice Soup

6. Skim.

7. Cook over low heat for 60–90 minutes.

Crapiata Materana

Ingredients

1/2 cup whole dried fava beans

4. Put the legumes, grains, and potatoes in a large pot.

7. Cook over low heat for about 45 minutes.

title: Fava Bean and Chicory Soup
instructions:
Fava Bean and Chicory Soup

Lucanian dried-fava purée with wild chicory sautéed with garlic and chile.

Ingredients

about 12 cups field chicory or catalogna

2 1/8 qt water for the fava beans
3 1/4 qt water for the chicory
1 2/3 tsp fine salt, divided

Preparation

1. Rinse the fava beans.

2. Soak in plenty of warm water overnight.

3. Drain.

4. Put the fava beans in a pot with the fresh water.

5. Bring to a gentle simmer.

6. Cook until completely soft, about 60–90 minutes.

7. Add about 2/3 teaspoon salt during the final 15 minutes.

8. Drain, reserving 1 cup cooking liquid.

11. Add the purée.

12. Cook for 3–4 minutes.

13. Clean and wash the chicory.

14. Bring the measured water to a boil with about 2/3 teaspoon salt.

15. Boil the chicory for 10–15 minutes, until tender.

16. Drain and squeeze dry.

17. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a second skillet.

18. Add the remaining garlic and chile.

19. Add the chicory.

20. Sauté for 5 minutes.

21. Add the remaining salt.

Service

Spoon the fava purée onto plates, add the chicory alongside, and finish with the remaining olive oil.

Chef's note

The fava purée should be thick but not dry; using its own cooking liquid preserves both flavor and starch.

instructions:
Chestnut and Bean Soup

Rustic chestnut-and-borlotti soup with pancetta, garlic, and tomato.

Mashing only part of the beans thickens the soup while preserving whole pieces and a rustic texture.

title: Calabrian Vegetable Soup
instructions:
Calabrian Vegetable Soup

Calabrian millecosedde with mixed legumes, Savoy cabbage, dried mushrooms, pancetta, tomato, pasta, and ’nduja.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

1 cup mixed dried legumes such as fava beans, chickpeas, beans, and lentils
1 celery stalk, divided

1 carrot, divided
about 3/4 cup finely chopped pancetta
about 4 cups sliced Savoy cabbage

2 ripe San Marzano tomatoes or peeled tomatoes, crushed

about 3 cups small pasta such as ditalini
4 1/4 cups reserved legume cooking liquid
1 1/4 tsp fine salt
3/4 cup finely grated Pecorino
1 tsp ’nduja

Preparation

1. Soak the legumes in cold water for 12 hours.

2. Drain and rinse.

3. Put the legumes in a pot with half of the carrot, half of the celery, and half of the onion.

4. Cover with plenty of water.

5. Cook for about 45 minutes.

6. Drain while still al dente, reserving at least the measured cooking liquid.

7. Soak the dried mushrooms in warm water for 20 minutes.

8. Drain and chop coarsely.

9. Heat 3 tablespoons olive oil in an earthenware or heavy pot.

10. Add the pancetta and garlic.

11. Brown for 4–5 minutes.

12. Remove the garlic.

13. Finely chop the remaining onion, celery, and carrot.

14. Add them to the pot.

15. Cook for 5 minutes.

16. Add the tomatoes.

17. Pour in the reserved legume broth.

18. Bring to a boil.

19. Add the cabbage, legumes, and mushrooms.

20. Add the salt.

21. Cover.

22. Cook over low heat for 1 hour.

23. Add the pasta.

24. Cook until al dente, stirring often.

25. Turn off the heat.

26. Stir in the ’nduja.

Service

Finish with Pecorino and the remaining olive oil.

Chef's note

Adding the ’nduja off the heat keeps its chile and cured-meat aroma more distinct.

instructions:
Calabrian Licurdia

Calabrian red-Tropea-onion and potato soup with caciocavallo, Pecorino, and croutons.

6 red Tropea onions, sliced

2. Add the water.

3. Add the salt and half of the chile flakes.

5. Cover.

15. Rest for 2 minutes so the cheese begins to melt.

Chef's note

Pouring the boiling soup directly over the caciocavallo lets the cheese soften and stretch without a second cooking step.

title: Tropea Onion Soup
instructions:
Tropea Onion Soup

Calabrian red Tropea onion cream soup with tomato, Parmigiano, basil, and mullet bottarga.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

about 8 cups thinly sliced red Tropea onions
2/3 cup tomato passata
1 1/2 cups finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano
4 1/4 cups hot vegetable broth
14 tbsp butter
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
10 basil leaves
1 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
about 3 tbsp finely grated or thinly sliced mullet bottarga

Preparation

1. Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot.

2. Add the onions.

3. Add half of the salt.

4. Cook gently for 15–20 minutes, stirring often, until very soft without browning.

5. Add the tomato passata.

6. Cook for 5–7 minutes.

7. Add 2 cups plus 2 tablespoons hot broth.

8. Cover partially.

9. Cook over low heat for 20 minutes.

10. Add the remaining broth.

11. Continue for another 10–20 minutes, until the onions are completely soft.

12. Add the Parmigiano.

13. Blend with an immersion blender until smooth.

14. Add the remaining salt and pepper.

15. Return to low heat for 2 minutes.

Service

Divide among bowls and finish with basil and bottarga.

Chef's note

Cooking the onions slowly without browning preserves the characteristic sweetness of Tropea onions and keeps the soup's flavor clean.

title: Calabrian Chickpea Soup
instructions:
Calabrian Chickpea Soup

Calabrian chickpea-and-tomato soup with lagane pasta, garlic, parsley, rosemary, and chile.

Ingredients

about 2 cups lagane or semolina pasta

1. Soak the chickpeas in plenty of cold water for 48 hours.

2. Drain and rinse.

3. Put the chickpeas, onion, and celery in an earthenware or heavy pot.

4. Add the water.

5. Bring to a boil.

6. Reduce the heat.

7. Cook for about 40 minutes, or until the chickpeas are tender.

8. Add half of the salt during the final 10 minutes.

9. Drain the chickpeas, reserving 2 cups plus 2 tablespoons cooking liquid.

10. Pass half of the chickpeas through a food mill.

11. Keep the remaining chickpeas whole.

12. Heat about 3 tbsp plus 1 tsp olive oil in a saucepan.

13. Add the garlic, parsley, and rosemary.

15. Add the tomatoes and chile.

16. Add the remaining salt.

20. Cook for 10 minutes.

21. Boil the lagane in salted water until al dente.

22. Drain directly into the chickpea sauce.

23. Stir for 2 minutes.

24. If needed, add the remaining chickpea liquid in small portions to keep the soup creamy.

Chef's note

Puréeing only half of the chickpeas creates a creamy base while preserving whole beans for texture.

title: Fava Bean Macco
instructions:
Fava Bean Macco

Sicilian dried-fava macco slowly cooked with onion, carrot, celery, and wild fennel.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

2 1/2 cups dried split fava beans
1 onion, finely chopped
2 carrots, finely chopped
1 celery stalk, finely chopped
1/3 cup finely chopped wild fennel, divided
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, divided
2 2/3 qt water
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

For the optional pasta version
about 1 1/4 cups broken spaghetti or ditalini

Preparation

1. Rinse the fava beans.

2. Soak them in plenty of cold water for 12 hours.

3. Drain and rinse.

4. Put the fava beans in a pot.

5. Add the water.

6. Add half of the wild fennel.

7. Bring to a boil.

8. Skim.

9. Reduce the heat.

10. Cook without salt for 2–3 hours, until the beans begin breaking down.

11. Heat 3 tablespoons olive oil in a second saucepan.

12. Add the onion, carrots, and celery.

13. Cook for 8–10 minutes.

14. Add the remaining wild fennel.

15. Drain the fava beans, reserving 6 1/3 cups cooking liquid.

16. Add the fava beans to the sautéed vegetables.

17. Add 2 cups plus 2 tablespoons cooking liquid.

18. Add the salt.

19. Cook over low heat for about 1 hour, stirring often.

20. Add more reserved cooking liquid in 1/2-cup portions if the macco becomes too thick before the beans have fully broken down.

21. Mash some of the fava beans against the side of the pot with a wooden spoon.

22. For the pasta version, add the pasta once the macco is creamy and cook until al dente, adding reserved fava liquid if needed.

23. Add the pepper.

Service

Finish with the remaining olive oil.

Chef's note

Traditional macco should be thick and slightly coarse, not completely smooth like a modern puréed soup.

title: St. Joseph Fava Bean Macco
instructions:
St. Joseph Fava Bean Macco

Traditional Sicilian St. Joseph macco with dried fava beans, onion, celery, and wild fennel.

Yield: 6–8 servings

Ingredients

4 cups dried split fava beans
1 onion, finely chopped
1 celery stalk, finely chopped
1/2 cup finely chopped wild fennel
3 1/4 qt water
5 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Optional traditional variations
about 8 cups cooked squeezed chard
about 1 2/3 cups ditalini or broken spaghetti

Preparation

1. Rinse the fava beans thoroughly.

2. Soak in plenty of cold water for at least 12 hours.

3. Drain and rinse.

4. Put the fava beans in a large pot.

5. Add the onion, celery, and wild fennel.

6. Add the water.

7. Bring to a boil.

8. Skim away any foam.

9. Reduce the heat.

10. Cook without salt for 50–60 minutes.

11. Once the fava beans begin breaking down, add the salt.

12. Continue for another 15–30 minutes, stirring frequently.

13. Mash some of the beans against the side of the pot until thick and rustic.

14. If the macco becomes too thick, add hot water in 1/2-cup portions until the desired consistency is reached.

15. For the chard variation, add the cooked chard during the final 5 minutes.

16. For the pasta variation, add the pasta once the macco is already creamy and cook until al dente, stirring frequently.

17. Turn off the heat.

18. Stir in 4 tablespoons olive oil.

19. Add the pepper.

Macco is traditionally associated with St. Joseph's Day and should remain a rustic creamy purée; it does not need to be blended completely.

title: Tenerumi Soup
instructions:
Tenerumi Soup

Sicilian tender squash-leaf soup with tomato and broken linguine.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

2 bunches tenerumi, about 16 tender vines
10–12 ripe tomatoes, about 5 1/3 cups chopped
2 garlic cloves
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
about 3 1/2 cups broken linguine
2 2/3 qt water
1 2/3 tsp fine salt, divided
4 1/4 cups ice water for cooling the tomatoes

Preparation

1. Remove only the tender leaves from the tenerumi vines.

2. Wash thoroughly.

3. Bring the water to a boil with about 1 teaspoon salt.

4. Add the tenerumi.

5. Cook for 8–10 minutes.

6. Leave the tenerumi in their cooking water.

7. Bring a second pot of water to a boil.

8. Score the tomatoes with a cross.

9. Blanch for 2 minutes.

10. Transfer immediately to the ice water.

11. Peel the tomatoes.

12. Chop coarsely.

13. Heat the olive oil in a third saucepan.

14. Add the garlic.

15. Cook for 1 minute.

16. Add the tomatoes.

17. Add the remaining salt.

18. Cook for 10–15 minutes, until the tomatoes soften.

19. Break the linguine into pieces 1 1/2–2 inches long.

20. Add the tomato mixture to the pot with the tenerumi and their cooking water.

21. Return to a boil.

22. Add the pasta.

23. Cook until al dente, stirring often.

24. Remove the garlic.

Service

Serve immediately in soup bowls.

Chef's note

Cooking the pasta directly in the tenerumi water keeps both the vegetable flavor and the pasta starch in the finished soup.

instructions:
Sicilian Chickpea Soup

22. Remove the bay leaf and rosemary.

Adding the carrots and celery after the chickpeas' first hour of cooking prevents the vegetables from completely breaking down.

title: Catania Fish Soup
instructions:
Catania Fish Soup

Catania fish soup with broth made from fish heads and bones, tomato, white wine, celery, onion, garlic, and toasted bread.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

2 1/4 lb mixed fish for soup
3 1/3 cups peeled seeded tomatoes

1 garlic clove, minced
1 large onion, thinly sliced and divided
1 celery stalk, cut into pieces
1 bay leaf
3/4 cup plus 1 tbsp dry white wine
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp olive oil
5 1/4 cups water
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
4 slices stale rustic bread

Preparation

1. Scale, gut, and wash the fish.

2. Fillet the larger fish, reserving the heads and bones.

3. Cut the flesh into even pieces.

4. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a saucepan.

5. Add half of the onion.

6. Cook for 3 minutes.

7. Add the fish heads and bones.

8. Brown for about 10 minutes.

9. Add the water.

10. Add the celery and half of the salt.

11. Cover.

12. Cook for about 30 minutes.

13. Strain the broth carefully.

14. Preheat the oven to 375°F.

15. Put the tomatoes, parsley, garlic, remaining onion, and bay leaf in an earthenware baking vessel.

16. Arrange the fish pieces, starting with the firmest varieties.

17. Add the pepper and remaining salt.

18. Pour in the wine and remaining olive oil.

19. Add enough strained broth to nearly cover the fish.

20. Cover the vessel.

21. Bake for about 40 minutes.

22. Toast the bread.

Service

Put one toast slice in each soup bowl and ladle the fish and broth over it.

Chef's note

Layering delicate fish above firmer varieties helps prevent them from breaking apart during oven cooking.

title: Messina-style Mussel Soup
instructions:
Messina-style Mussel Soup

Sicilian mussel soup with tomato, onion, celery, chile, thyme, parsley, and lemon zest.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

2 1/4 lb mussels
1 tbsp corn oil
1 fresh chile, minced
1 white onion, finely chopped
3 celery stalks, finely chopped
1 garlic clove, minced
2 2/3 cups chopped ripe tomatoes
1 bay leaf
1 tbsp fresh thyme
1/3 cup finely chopped fresh parsley
finely grated zest of 1 lemon
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1 1/4 cups water, plus enough cold water to bring the strained mussel liquid to exactly 1 3/4 cups total

Preparation

1. Scrub and clean the mussels thoroughly.

2. Put them in a wide saucepan.

3. Add 1 1/4 cups water.

4. Cover.

5. Bring to a boil.

6. Cook over low heat for 3–5 minutes, until the mussels open.

7. Discard any that remain closed.

8. Drain the mussels, reserving all of the liquid.

9. Remove most mussels from their shells, leaving 4 in the shell for garnish.

10. Strain the cooking liquid carefully.

11. Measure it and add cold water until you have exactly 1 3/4 cups total liquid.

12. Heat the corn oil in a saucepan.

13. Add the chile, onion, celery, and garlic.

14. Cook over low heat for 5 minutes.

15. Add the measured mussel liquid, tomatoes, bay leaf, thyme, and pepper.

16. Bring to a boil.

17. Cover.

18. Cook over low heat for 25 minutes.

19. Add the shelled mussels.

20. Cook for another 5 minutes.

21. Remove the bay leaf.

Service

Divide among bowls and finish each serving with one mussel in its shell, parsley, and lemon zest.

Chef's note

Do not add salt before the final tasting; the natural mussel liquid is normally already quite salty.

Favata Sarda

Traditional Sardinian fava-bean soup with sausage, pork ribs, pork rind, wild fennel, and carasau bread.

about 3 1/3 cups sliced Sardinian sausage
about 3 1/3 cups pork-rib pieces

1 red chile

6. Bring to a boil.

11. Reduce the heat.

12. Cook slowly for about 2 hours, stirring occasionally.

13. Add hot water if the level drops too far.

14. Remove the chile and garlic.

15. Adjust with the remaining salt.

Chef's note

Favata benefits from a long gentle simmer so collagen from the rind and ribs gives body to the broth.

Fregola Soup

1. Soak the clams in lightly salted water for about 2 hours.

2. Rinse thoroughly.

3. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a wide skillet.

5. Add the clams.

6. Cover and cook over high heat until they open.

10. Remove about two-thirds of the clams from their shells.

15. Add the onion.

16. Add 1 tablespoon warm water.

17. Cook for about 5 minutes.

18. Add the sun-dried tomatoes.

19. Add the fregola.

20. Toast for 2–3 minutes.

21. Add the strained clam liquid.

22. Gradually add hot broth.

23. Cook the fregola until al dente, about 12–15 minutes.

24. During the final 3 minutes, add the shelled clams.

25. Add the cherry tomatoes if using.

26. Add half of the chopped parsley.

Clam liquid is naturally salty, so strain it carefully and add salt only after tasting the finished soup.

5. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a pot.

6. Add the onion, sage, and rosemary.

9. Add the hot broth.

18. Remove half of the chickpeas.

20. Return the purée to the pot.

21. Stir into the whole chickpeas.

Service

Blending half of the chickpeas creates a creamy texture while leaving enough whole legumes for structure.

instructions:
Dried Fava Soup

Puglian dried-fava soup with wild chicory and sivoni, white wine, garlic, and chile.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1 1/2 cups dried split fava beans
about 20 cups wild chicory and sivoni greens
2 garlic cloves
1 red onion, finely chopped
6 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided
2/3 cup dry white wine, divided
1 small chile
1 tsp crushed pink peppercorns
4 1/4 cups water
1 tbsp plus 1 tsp coarse salt
2 slices Altamura bread

Preparation

1. Soak the fava beans in cold water for at least 8 hours.

2. Drain and rinse.

3. Clean the chicory and sivoni thoroughly, removing tough parts.

4. Heat 3 tablespoons olive oil in a pot.

5. Add the crushed garlic and half of the chile.

6. Cook for 1 minute.

7. Add the chicory and sivoni.

8. Add half of the coarse salt.

9. Cover.

10. Cook until the greens begin to wilt, about 10 minutes.

11. In another saucepan, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil.

12. Add the onion.

13. Cook for 5 minutes.

14. Add 1/3 cup wine.

15. Let it evaporate.

16. Add the fava beans.

17. Add the pink peppercorns and remaining salt.

18. Add the remaining wine.

19. Let it evaporate.

20. Add the wilted greens.

21. Add the water.

22. Cover.

23. Cook over low heat for about 30 minutes, until the fava beans are tender.

24. Toast the bread.

Service

Finish with the remaining olive oil, remaining chile, and toasted bread.

Chef's note

Cooking the fava beans and greens separately first lets each develop its own flavor before they are combined in the soup.

title: Puglian-style Onion Soup
instructions:
Puglian-style Onion Soup

Gratinated onion soup with sage, Puglian bread, and Gruyère.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

4 onions
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil
3 1/2 tbsp butter
16 sage leaves
4 tbsp all-purpose flour
4 1/4 cups hot vegetable broth
1/2 cup finely grated Gruyère
4 slices Puglian-style bread
3/4 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Thinly slice the onions.

2. Melt the butter in a pot.

3. Add 3 tablespoons olive oil.

4. Add the sage and onions.

5. Cook gently for 5–6 minutes.

6. Add the flour.

7. Stir for 1–2 minutes.

8. Add 3 cups plus 3 tablespoons hot broth.

9. Cover.

10. Cook for 10 minutes.

11. Add the salt and pepper.

12. Add the remaining broth.

13. Cook for another 10 minutes.

14. Heat the remaining olive oil in a skillet.

15. Toast the bread slices for a few minutes per side.

16. Preheat a conventional oven to 400°F.

17. Divide the soup among 4 ovenproof crocks.

18. Put one bread slice in each.

19. Add 2 tablespoons Gruyère to each serving.

20. Add black pepper.

21. Bake for 10 minutes.

22. Broil for another 2 minutes.

Service

Rest for 2–3 minutes and serve.

Chef's note

Briefly cooking the flour with the onions removes its raw flavor and thickens the soup without lumps.

title: Zuppa Pavese
instructions:
Zuppa Pavese

Pavia-style soup with butter-browned stale bread, eggs, Grana Padano, and boiling meat broth.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

4 1/4 cups meat broth
8 slices stale bread
3 tbsp butter
8 large eggs
1/3 cup finely grated Grana Padano
2/3 tsp fine salt, only if the broth is not already well seasoned
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Bring the broth to a gentle boil.

2. Taste and add the salt only if needed.

3. Melt the butter in a large nonstick skillet.

4. Add the bread slices.

5. Brown on both sides, keeping them crisp outside and still soft in the center.

6. Put 2 bread slices in each heatproof soup bowl.

7. Crack 2 eggs over the bread in each bowl, keeping the yolks intact.

8. Sprinkle with Grana Padano.

9. Pour the boiling broth around the sides of each bowl rather than directly over the eggs.

10. Add the pepper.

11. If the whites remain too raw, place the bowls in a preheated 300°F oven for 2–4 minutes, until the whites are just set.

Service

Serve immediately.

Chef's note

Pouring the broth around the edge of the bowl cooks the egg gently without breaking the yolk.

title: Milanese Minestrone
instructions:
Milanese Minestrone

Long-cooked Milanese minestrone with rice, Savoy cabbage, vegetables, borlotti beans, pork rind, aromatic lard, and Grana.

Yield: 10 servings

Ingredients

1 2/3 cups Originario or Maratelli rice
1 medium Savoy cabbage, thinly sliced
1 zucchini, diced
4 carrots, diced
1 leafy celery bunch, about 4 cups chopped
about 2 1/4 cups peeled small onions
3 medium potatoes, peeled and left whole
about 2 cups fresh borlotti beans or 1/2 cup dried beans, soaked
about 1 2/3 cups cleaned precooked pork rind
about 2/3 cup finely chopped lard
1/3 cup fresh parsley
1 garlic clove, germ removed
8 sage leaves
1 ripe tomato, seeded and diced
20 fresh basil leaves
4 1/4 qt water, plus 4 1/4 cups boiling water available if needed
2 1/2 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper
1 1/2 cups finely grated Grana Padano

Preparation

1. If using dried borlotti beans, soak them for 12 hours.

2. Finely chop the lard, parsley, and garlic together into a paste.

3. Put the carrots, celery, onions, potatoes, beans, pork rind, sage, and lard mixture in a very large pot.

4. Add the cold water.

5. Bring slowly to a boil.

6. Add about 1 2/3 teaspoons salt.

7. Reduce the heat.

8. Cook very slowly for about 3 hours.

9. Add the Savoy cabbage.

10. Continue for 40–60 minutes, until the cabbage is tender.

11. If the liquid level falls too far, add boiling water in 1-cup portions.

12. Add the zucchini.

13. Add the rice 20 minutes before the end.

14. Cook, stirring frequently.

15. Mash the potatoes against the side of the pot to thicken the broth.

16. Add the tomato and basil during the final 5 minutes.

17. Add the pepper.

18. Add the remaining salt only if needed.

Service

Serve very hot with plenty of Grana Padano.

Chef's note

The long cooking naturally thickens the broth; mashing the potatoes completes the texture without flour.

instructions:
Rice and Parsley Soup

Lombardy rice soup with broth, onion, parsley, butter, and Grana Padano.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1 1/2 cups Originario or Ribe rice
5 1/2 cups meat or vegetable broth
1/2 cup finely chopped fresh parsley, divided
1 small onion, finely chopped
2 tbsp butter
1/3 cup plus 1 tbsp finely grated Grana Padano
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
3/4 tsp fine salt, only if the broth is not already well seasoned
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Bring the broth almost to a boil.

3. Add the onion.

4. Cook over low heat for 5–6 minutes without browning.

5. Add the hot broth.

6. Taste and add the salt only if needed.

7. Bring to a boil.

8. Add the rice.

9. Cook over medium-low heat for 15–18 minutes, stirring every 3–4 minutes.

10. Three minutes before the end, add about three-quarters of the parsley.

11. Turn off the heat.

12. Add the Grana Padano.

13. Stir.

14. Cover and rest for 2 minutes.

Adding the parsley only during the final minutes preserves its fresh color and herbal aroma.

Rice, Milk, and Chestnut Soup

Creamy chestnut-and-rice soup with whole milk and butter.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

about 1 1/2 cups fresh chestnuts
3/4 cup rice for soup
2 cups plus 2 tbsp whole milk
2 1/8 qt water
2 tbsp butter
1 1/4 tsp fine salt

Preparation

1. Score the chestnut shells.

2. Discard any damaged chestnuts.

3. Put them in a pot with cold water.

4. Bring to a boil.

5. Cook for 5 minutes.

6. Drain only a few chestnuts at a time.

7. Peel them while still hot, removing the inner skin as well.

8. Put the peeled chestnuts in a pot with the measured water.

9. Bring to a boil.

10. Add the salt.

11. Cook over medium heat for about 2 hours 30 minutes, until the chestnuts are very tender.

12. Add the rice.

13. Cook for half of the rice's required cooking time.

14. Heat the milk without boiling.

15. Add it to the soup.

16. Continue cooking until the rice is tender and the soup is well bound.

17. Turn off the heat.

18. Add the butter.

19. Stir until fully melted.

Service

Rest for 2 minutes and serve very hot.

Chef's note

Adding the milk only halfway through the rice cooking prevents prolonged boiling that could make it stick to the bottom.

instructions:
Lombard Onion Soup

Lombardy-style onion soup with slowly stewed onions, butter, sage, white wine, flour, and broth.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

about 8 cups thinly sliced white or yellow onions
5 tbsp unsalted butter
1/3 cup all-purpose flour
6 fresh sage leaves, finely chopped
1/2 cup dry white wine
6 1/3 cups hot meat broth
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

For serving
6 slices rustic bread
2/3 cup finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano

Preparation

1. Melt the butter in a heavy saucepan over low heat.

2. Add the onions.

3. Cover.

4. Cook slowly for about 50 minutes, stirring every 8–10 minutes, until soft and only lightly golden.

5. Add the flour and sage.

6. Add the salt and pepper.

7. Stir and cook for 4 minutes.

8. Pour in the white wine.

9. Cook for 2–3 minutes, until the wine is nearly evaporated.

10. Gradually add the hot broth while stirring.

11. Bring to a boil.

12. Reduce the heat.

13. Cook uncovered for 25–30 minutes.

14. Toast the bread.

15. Put one slice in each bowl.

Service

Ladle the boiling soup over the bread and finish with Parmigiano.

Chef's note

The long initial stewing turns the onions soft and sweet without requiring deep caramelization.

instructions:
Busecca

Milanese tripe stew with pancetta, white beans, aromatic vegetables, tomato, and sage.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

1 1/8 lb cleaned precooked tripe, cut into strips
about 3/4 cup diced pancetta
about 1 1/4 cups cooked large white beans
1 carrot, finely chopped
1 onion, finely chopped
1 celery stalk, finely chopped
2 tbsp butter
3 tbsp tomato passata
4 sage leaves
4 1/4 cups hot water
1 bouillon cube, about 2 tsp
3/4 tsp fine salt, only if needed
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Melt the butter in a saucepan.

2. Add the onion, carrot, celery, pancetta, and sage.

3. Cook over medium-low heat for 8–10 minutes.

4. Add the tripe.

5. Increase the heat slightly.

6. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until the tripe loses its surface moisture.

7. Add the passata.

8. Add the bouillon.

9. Add the pepper.

10. Pour in 3 cups plus 3 tablespoons hot water.

11. Bring to a gentle simmer.

12. Cover partially.

13. Cook over moderate heat for 1 hour.

14. Stir every 10 minutes.

15. If the sauce becomes too dry, add the remaining 1 cup water in two portions.

16. Add the beans.

17. Cook for another 15–20 minutes, stirring gently.

18. Taste and add the salt only if needed.

Service

Serve very hot.

Chef's note

The bouillon, pancetta, and beans can already provide considerable salinity, so adjust the salt only at the end.

title: Valpelline Soup
instructions:
Valpelline Soup

Aosta Valley seupa à la Vapelenentse with rye bread, Savoy cabbage, Fontina, broth, and butter.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

about 8 cups shredded Savoy cabbage
about 2 1/2 cups sliced or diced Fontina
about 6 cups rye-bread slices, about 3/8 inch thick
3 1/2 tbsp butter, divided
5 cups hot meat broth
3/4 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

2. Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a skillet.

3. Add the cabbage.

4. Add 1/2 cup broth.

5. Add the salt.

6. Cover.

7. Stew for about 10 minutes, until the cabbage begins to soften.

8. Lightly butter a baking dish with about 2 teaspoons butter.

9. Make one layer of bread.

10. Cover with some of the cabbage.

11. Add a layer of Fontina.

12. Add pepper.

13. Repeat the layers, finishing with Fontina.

14. Slowly pour the remaining hot broth around the edges until the bread is well moistened but not floating.

15. Dot the top with the remaining butter.

16. Bake for 20–25 minutes, until the cheese is melted and the surface lightly gratinated.

Service

Rest for 5–10 minutes and serve very hot.

Chef's note

Adding the broth slowly lets the bread absorb it without completely losing its structure.

Cogne Soup

Aosta Valley soup of rye bread, Arborio rice, and Fontina, gratinated with butter.

Yield: 4 servings

Ingredients

about 2 cups sliced Fontina
1 cup Arborio rice
7 tbsp butter, divided

1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Bring the broth to a boil.

2. Add the rice.

3. Cook for about 15 minutes, leaving it very al dente.

4. Drain the rice, reserving all of the broth.

5. Melt about 5 tablespoons butter in a skillet.

6. Cut the rye bread into slices.

7. Brown the slices in the butter on both sides.

8. Arrange one layer of bread in a heatproof serving dish.

9. Add a layer of rice.

10. Add a layer of Fontina.

11. Repeat the layers, finishing with Fontina.

12. Slowly pour in the hot broth until all layers are well moistened.

13. Rest for 20 minutes.

14. Preheat the broiler.

15. Dot the top with the remaining butter.

16. Add the pepper.

17. Broil for about 10 minutes.

Service

Rest for 5 minutes and serve very hot.

Chef's note

Resting before gratinating lets the bread absorb the broth and allows the rice to complete its hydration gently.

title: Ajucche Soup
instructions:
Ajucche Soup

Piedmont soup with ajucche greens, stale bread, pork ribs, pig's foot, sausage, toma, and Parmigiano.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

about 2 1/4 lb cleaned ajucche greens
7 tbsp butter, divided
about 7/16 lb pork ribs
1 cleaned pig's foot
about 1 cup crumbled sausage
about 2 cups finely grated Parmigiano
about 1 2/3 cups sliced toma cheese
about 12 cups stale rustic bread slices, about 3/8 inch thick
6 1/3 cups water
1 1/3 tsp fine salt
1 tsp freshly ground black pepper

Preparation

1. Bring the water to a boil.

2. Add the pork ribs and pig's foot.

3. Add half of the salt.

4. Simmer gently for about 45 minutes.

5. Remove the meats from the broth.

6. Strain the broth.

7. Return it to a boil.

8. Add the ajucche.

9. Cook for about 5 minutes.

10. Drain the greens, reserving all of the broth.

11. Cook the sausage in a dry skillet for 5–7 minutes.

12. Cool slightly.

13. Melt about 3 1/2 tablespoons butter in a skillet.

14. Toast the bread slices on both sides.

15. Butter a deep earthenware baking dish with about 1 1/2 tablespoons butter.

16. Make one layer of ajucche.

17. Cover with toasted bread.

18. Add Parmigiano, sausage, toma, pepper, and small pieces of butter.

19. Moisten with several ladles of broth.

20. Repeat the layers until all ingredients are used.

21. Finish with bread, cheese, and the remaining butter.

22. Add enough broth to keep the soup soft but not liquid.

23. Preheat the oven to 300°F.

24. Bake for 50–55 minutes.

Service

Rest for 10 minutes and serve very hot.

Chef's note

title: Cisrà
instructions:
Cisrà

Langhe tripe-and-chickpea soup with leeks, carrots, potatoes, celery, onion, and optional sage.

Yield: 6–8 servings

Ingredients

about 3 cups cleaned precooked tripe pieces
1 1/2 cups dried chickpeas
3 leeks, sliced
2 carrots, diced
2 potatoes, diced
2 celery stalks, diced
1 onion, finely chopped
1 garlic clove, optional
2 sage leaves, optional
3 1/4 qt water
1 2/3 tsp fine salt
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil

Preparation

1. The night before, soak the chickpeas in plenty of cold water.

2. The next day, drain and rinse.

3. Put the chickpeas, tripe, leeks, carrots, potatoes, celery, and onion in a large pot.

4. Add the water.

5. Bring slowly to a boil.

6. Reduce the heat.

7. Cover partially.

8. Cook very slowly for at least 2 hours 30 minutes and up to 3 hours.

9. Stir every 20–30 minutes.

10. If the liquid drops too low before the chickpeas are tender, add boiling water in 1-cup portions.

11. Add the salt during the final 20 minutes.

12. For the aromatic version, heat the olive oil in a small skillet.

13. Add the garlic and sage.

14. Cook for 1–2 minutes.

15. Remove the garlic.

16. Pour the flavored oil into the soup.

Service

Rest for 5 minutes and serve very hot.

Chef's note

Long gentle cooking makes the tripe tender while the chickpeas naturally thicken the broth.

title: Supa Barbetta
instructions:
Supa Barbetta

Waldensian Piedmont soup with breadsticks, meat broth, Parmigiano or toma, butter, cinnamon, and nutmeg.

Yield: 6 servings

Ingredients

about 12 cups broken plain breadsticks
4 1/4 cups hot meat broth
about 2 cups finely grated Parmigiano or thinly sliced toma
7 tbsp fresh butter, divided
1/4 tsp ground cinnamon
1/4 tsp freshly grated nutmeg

Preparation

1. Melt half of the butter in a heatproof serving dish or shallow casserole.

2. Break the breadsticks into 2–3 pieces each.

3. Make one layer of breadsticks.

4. Sprinkle with some of the cheese.

5. Add a small amount of cinnamon and nutmeg.

6. Repeat the layers until all of the breadsticks and cheese are used.

7. Slowly pour in the hot broth.

8. Set over the lowest possible heat.

9. Cook without stirring until nearly all of the broth is absorbed.

10. During cooking, gently lift the breadsticks with a spatula if they begin sticking to the bottom.

11. Preheat the broiler.

12. Transfer the dish to the oven.

13. Broil for 10 minutes.

14. Melt the remaining butter.

15. Pour it over the soup immediately after broiling.

Service

Serve immediately.

Chef's note

Do not stir during cooking; the layers should remain distinct and the breadsticks should absorb the broth without becoming a purée.
